summary: Broad duodenal villi, crypt renewal and protective submucosal Brunner glands with continuous duct routes. Distinct blood/lymph and enteric-control lessons preserve the existing foundation.
scale_note: Schematic histology crop in authored model units; no verified universal physical calibration. Six representative broad villi have lateral dimensions enlarged approximately 1.6 times. Five Brunner lobules with fifteen enlarged terminals and sparse epithelial cells show relationships, not population counts. The gold brush border is an enlarged apical surface. Vessel colors show a teaching flow cue rather than literal blood color or an oxygen measurement.

description_overrides.Brunner glands: Brunner glands are branched mucous glands, predominantly submucosal and most abundant in proximal duodenum, with density decreasing distally. They deliver protective alkaline mucus through ducts into crypts and then the intestinal lumen. Direct gland bicarbonate output is not quantified here; surface epithelium and pancreatic secretion also contribute to acid neutralization. Five representative lobules with three enlarged terminals each show organization rather than gland density or one gland per crypt.
description_overrides.Brunner gland ducts: Brunner gland ducts cross the muscularis mucosae and open into crypt lumens. The represented recipient port lies above the blind crypt floor; it is not the entire crypt base. Front lobules and ducts lie on the Z=0 teaching cut to expose a continuous route; posterior lobules show a different position.
description_overrides.Crypt base stem cells (Lgr5+): Lgr5-positive crypt base columnar stem cells lie among Paneth cells and generate renewing epithelial lineages. Most villus epithelial cells migrate and turn over over several days; this does not mean all epithelial cell types are replaced together. Paneth cells remain in the crypt and live longer. Classic lineage-tracing evidence is from adult mice; the enlarged sparse cells here are a teaching representation.
description_overrides.Central lacteals: Central lacteals are blind-ended initial lymphatics in villus cores. Long-chain dietary lipids are processed in enterocytes into chylomicrons, released basolaterally into the interstitium and taken up across lacteal endothelium. Lymph then drains toward mesenteric lymphatics and eventually systemic venous blood. Chylomicron uptake depends on specialized lymphatic junctions; this is not simply a rigid particle-size sieve. Some lipid products use portal blood instead.
description_overrides.Submucosal venules: Submucosal venules collect mucosal blood, including absorbed water-soluble nutrients. Duodenal venous blood drains toward the portal circulation outside this specimen. This small wall specimen does not display the extra-wall portal route.
description_overrides.Mucosal venous branches: Mucosal venous branches carry blood from the villus/crypt microcirculation across the muscularis mucosae toward submucosal venules. They remain distinct from lacteal drainage.
description_overrides.Villus smooth muscle: Villus smooth-muscle strands participate in local villus movement, which can aid lymph transport. This is distinct from muscularis externa propulsion. The strands do not make the lacteal a contractile blood vessel, and this model does not quantify pumping.
description_overrides.Brush border (microvilli): Brush border: densely packed microvilli on the apical enterocyte surface support absorption and membrane digestion. This enlarged gold apical teaching layer is distinct from the pink enterocyte lining and is interrupted at goblet openings. It does not depict individual microvilli or establish a fixed numerical surface-area multiplier. Plicae, villi and microvilli are different scales; this proximal-style crop has no jejunal plica.
description_overrides.Serosa: Outer covering: the existing selector Serosa depicts a thin outer wall covering. Serosa is mesothelium with connective tissue on peritoneal surfaces; adventitia attaches retroperitoneal duodenal surfaces to surrounding tissue. This isolated wall crop does not identify a specific peritoneal face; the selector is preserved for compatibility, and should not imply serosa around every duodenal surface.
description_overrides.Muscularis mucosae: Muscularis mucosae: a thin smooth-muscle boundary below crypt-bearing mucosa and above the gland-bearing submucosa. It supports local mucosal movement, distinct from muscularis externa propulsion. Brunner ducts and mucosal blood/lymph conduits traverse fitted apertures in this boundary.
